    B: binding energy · U: mean orbital kinetic energy · N: electron occupancy · n: denominator divisor. Coefficients define df/dw = Σ cₚ/(1+w)ᵖ, p = 2…6; zero-pad unused terms. See Method & sources for normalization and limits.

    Paste orbital data (CSV)

    Header required: label,B,U,N. Optional: Q,n,double,c2,c3,c4,c5,c6. Energies in eV. Supply all five coefficient columns together or leave all blank.

    For a molecule outside NIST, supply B, U, and N from an electronic-structure calculation or a documented source. Use a vertical ionization energy for the outermost orbital when available. A chemical formula alone cannot determine these inputs.

    Published & imported measurements

    Published markers are loaded automatically for supported targets. NIST markers are approximate digitizations, not raw numerical measurements; inspect the original NIST graph to check coverage and omitted overlaps. Theory-only reference datasets are excluded.

    Overlay your own measured cross sections

    Paste measured total-ionization data as T_eV,sigma_A2, with an optional header. 1 Å² = 10⁻²⁰ m² = 10⁻¹⁶ cm². No experimental points have been digitized or invented from the paper.

    Compare cross-section ratios

    Dimensionless σA / σB at the same incident energy. Choose total models or measured ion channels independently.

    A total-ionization ratio between molecules is not an m/z signal ratio. A measured fragment-channel ratio is closer to the quantity in Krempl et al. Figure 1, but instrument response, abundance, energy spread, and background are still separate inputs. No extrapolation is made beyond measured ranges. Ratios with a zero or missing denominator are undefined.

    Ratio values & interpretation

    Exact measured-energy matching is the default. Interpolated measurements are explicitly labeled estimates and drawn with dashed lines; they are not predictions of fragmentation. NIST markers are approximate plot digitizations, with imperfect energy coordinates, so exact matching between independent datasets may yield no common energies. Model curves use the current BEB convention and double-ionization setting. Current edited target follows your orbital inputs. Lower-bound selected-ion sums do not generally imply a bound on their ratio. No statistical ratio uncertainty is inferred from the authors’ overall precision estimates.

    Model equations & provenance

    Implements the total direct-ionization equations in Stone & Kim (2005), Eqs. 1–3. The initial hydrogen view follows Figure 1's axes and units; it is a model reconstruction, not a digitization of its curves or measurements.

    t = T/B; u = U/B; S = 4πa₀² N (R/B)²
    a₀ = 0.52918 Å; R = 13.6057 eV
    A(t) = 1 − 1/t − ln(t)/(t+1)
    BEB = S/[t+(u+1)/n] × [Q ln(t)(1−1/t²)/2 + (2−Q)A(t)]
    BED = S/(t+u+1) × [D(t) ln(t) + (2−Nᵢ/N)A(t)]
    D(t) = (1/N) ∫₀^((t−1)/2) [df/dw]/(1+w) dw
    Nᵢ = ∫₀^∞ df/dw dw; w = W/B
    df/dw = Σₚ₌₂⁶ cₚ/(1+w)ᵖ
    Nᵢ = Σ cₚ/(p−1); D(t) = Σ cₚ[1−(1+(t−1)/2)⁻ᵖ]/(pN)

    Cross sections are zero for T ≤ B. Coefficient integrals are evaluated analytically. Q = 1 is the paper's BEB Eq. 1; the alternate setting uses tabulated NIST Q. The n correction applies only to BEB (paper Eq. 4 / NIST introduction); this tool disables BED if any n ≠ 1 rather than silently extending BED to ionic or corrected targets. Double flags, when enabled, multiply each flagged orbital contribution by two. These are counting-cross-section estimates.

    What is bundled?

    Snapshot date: 19 October 2026. All orbital constants and NIST row remarks are retained in the accompanying JSON download. The snapshot is fixed, with no runtime request to NIST. Missing/empty orbital pages: CHO, CH₂O, C₂H₃O, SF₄, SF₅. Some NIST tables list only selected orbitals; “total” here means the sum of included rows. Inspect coverage before high-energy use.

    H and He BED coefficients are NIST continuum polynomial fits, using the orbital B and U listed in the atomic tables. H₂ uses the Kim–Rudd fit reproduced in Fedus & Karwasz (2019), Appendix C, Eq. C4. Nᵢ is computed from each polynomial, without renormalizing it to N. The separate 0.955 rescaling mentioned on NIST's hydrogen SDCS output is not applied to the paper's raw total BED equation here. The H fit has a small negative far-tail artifact; it is retained as published and is not a general-purpose photoionization spectrum.

    Custom input checks & interpretation

    Require B > 0, U ≥ 0, N > 0, 0 ≤ Q ≤ 2, integer n ≥ 1, finite numbers, and at least one orbital. BED needs a complete continuum fit for every included orbital, with 0 < Nᵢ ≤ N. User polynomials are checked for negative values over the sampled physical W range; supplied fits are not automatically validated against experiment. If a continuum fit is unavailable, no BED curve or mixed BEB/BED sum is shown.

    BEB agreement for targets in NIST is typically reported as 5–20% up to about 1 keV, not an uncertainty guarantee for a new target. The 1–10 keV interval is exploratory; the nonrelativistic model should not be used above 10 keV. This tool excludes autoionization (relevant to the paper's C and Al examples), resonances, neutral dissociation, and relativistic corrections.

    Added literature data

    Acetone orbital inputs: Prajapati et al. (2021), Table 7, PDF p. 14 / journal p. 13, RHF/cc-pVTZ. All 16 occupied orbitals (32 electrons) were transcribed and visually checked. The standard BEB equation above is used; the source's Eq. 8 has apparent typographical inconsistencies.

    Acetone measured channels: Vacher et al. (2008), Table 2, p. 121, at 12, 25 and 86 eV. IPA channels: Vacher et al. (2006), Table 1, p. 590, at 15, 50 and 86 eV. Units 10⁻¹⁶ cm² equal Å² numerically. Dashes are missing/unreported entries, not zeros. Selected-ion sums are derived from the tabulated entries; missing channels make low-energy sums lower bounds. The acetone 12 eV scale depends on BEB normalization and is not independent model validation. IPA total ionization: Hudson et al. (2003), Table 1, p. 3164, 48 tabulated points from 16–207 eV. The measured peak is 10.24 Å² at 93 eV; Table 2 reports a BEB peak of 9.48 Å² (−7.4%). Neither supplied IPA paper tabulates orbital B/U inputs; IPA remains data-only. Reproducibility better than ±2% is distinct from absolute accuracy (authors discuss a previously determined ±4% maximum instrument error); near-threshold points have increased uncertainty and about 1.2 eV electron-energy FWHM.

    NIST experimental markers: when available, marker centers were approximately digitized from NIST's original comparison GIF, using its own BEB ASCII curve to calibrate the plot. A ±2-pixel reading allowance is stored per point; this is not an experimental confidence interval. Ambiguous or overlapping symbols are omitted. Graphs whose theoretical trace did not validate the calibration do not supply numerical markers; the original experimental comparison remains available. No raw experimental numeric table was found in NIST's BEB download. Digitized points should not be used as high-precision reference data.
